title: Segmented prompt collections for INT8/FP8 calibration and validation
creator: Ava Chen
description: Create a reproducible, workload-segmented collection of production prompts to be used as canonical calibration and validation sets for INT8 and FP8 quantization profile tuning. Goal is to produce repeatable slices that represent realistic token length distributions, error-sensitive slices (e.g., code completion, multi-step reasoning, embeddings), and low-frequency critical customer intents. The collections must be anonymized, versioned, and tied to a deterministic sampling map so experiments are comparable across kernel changes and runtime optimizations.
sampling_strategy: Stratified by workload slice: conversational, code, search queries, document summarization, and embeddings extraction.
Recency window: sample 60% from last 90 days, 30% from 91–365 days, 10% legacy to preserve long-tail behaviors.
Importance weighting: boost prompts with high customer impact flags (support tickets, SLA incidents) by factor 3 during sampling to ensure coverage of failure modes.
Length stratification: ensure token-length bands (<=32, 33-128, 129-512, >512) represented proportionally with explicit minimums per band.
Reservoir sampling with seeded RNG for reproducibility; per-slice seeds stored alongside manifest.
Noise/corruption control: filter out PII and automatically remove low-quality noisy logs using heuristics, but include a guarded noisy-slice for robustness tests.
Sample size targets: small calibration (~10k examples per slice) for rapid quant-profile tuning, and large validation (~100k) for final accuracy sweeps.
data_sources: internal: query logs + incident tags (support, eval-cases)
validation_plan: Offline metrics: delta-perplexity, token-error-rate, semantic-similarity (SBERT cosine), and instruction-following fidelity measured against golden outputs.
Pass thresholds: no more than 1.5% relative degradation in semantic similarity for INT8 vs FP16 baseline on critical slices; FP8 target within 1.0% if achieved.
Regression gating: any slice with >2% degradation triggers hold and manual triage by Applied ML.
Human-in-the-loop: label 500 examples per critical slice for blind eval comparing FP16 vs quantized output for correctness and hallucination rate.
CI integration: calibration jobs produce artifact manifest with checksums; validation job posts results to dashboard and creates a PR comment summarizing pass/fail.
rollout_plan: Stage 1: run calibration with INT8/FP8 profiles on canary models in staging and compare to FP16 baseline.
Stage 2: smoke tests with simulated traffic using the validation collection; monitor latency, throughput, and accuracy metrics.
Stage 3: gated rollout to 5% traffic with automatic rollback on metric breach for 30 minutes.
Stage 4: full rollout and archive final manifests for future audits and reproducibility.
